That said, as a technical challenge, you could try blocking the content you don't want with a firewall. It would be a useful exercise in network security/administration.

First you have to figure out what URLs the Xbox is connecting to, so you can block them. This is done by "sniffing" your own network traffic using wireshark. To do this, install some Linux distro on a spare laptop, install wireshark and set things up so the XBox connects to the laptop, and the laptop connects to the internet. Start capturing network packets with wireshark, turn on the XBox and try to find out what URLs are the ones you need to block (pray thay the Xbox doesn't make thousands of connections...). Then you blacklist the URLs in the firewall. This will take some trial and error to get right. You want to block the unwantd content, but keep most of the useful functionality of the XBox.

If your router doesn't have a firewall feature, you also need a device (a good router, spare laptop or Raspberry Pi) in your network with a firewall on it, through which you send the traffic. These are some good options for free firewall software, I'm not sure which is best: Pi-hole, OPNSense or pfSense. I left out a lot of details, this is going to take some effort, but it should be technically possible to block the unwanted content from your Xbox.
